51047813.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Pseudomonas putida KSI by surface plasmon resonance analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR Screening: Fragment screening was conducted in a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare, Piscataway, NJ). KSI was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip by the amine-coupling reaction or on a SA sensor chip after protein modification with an EZ-Link sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-biotin kit (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA). The fragments were injected at 200 μM and flow rate of 30 μL min−1 in PBS buffer supplemented with 5% DMSO. Negative and positive control experiments were performed periodically to confirm the stability of the protein on the sensor chip by injecting buffer and DOC (100 μM), respectively. A new sensor chip was prepared after screening every 384 compounds (one plate). The binding level of each fragment was determined with the Biacore T200 evaluation software using a standard solvent correction (4–8% DMSO in eight steps).
original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Equilibrium SPR: Dissociation constant (K_D) was determined by SPR. KSI immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip was tested with fragments at different concentrations in PBS buffer supplemented with 5% DMSO. K_D was calculated from the maximal response in equilibrium.

original_paragraph.Results section - SPR screening: The initial screening of an optimized library comprising 2000 compounds was performed by SPR on two different sensor chips: CM5 or SA (Figure 3a). Double screening reduces the number of false positives at the initial stage. The integrity of the sensor chip was checked periodically by injecting DOC. Response levels were corrected using standard methodologies. The binding responses were normalized with respect to DOC and buffer. Representative binding responses are shown in Figure 3b–e. Often, nonspecific and promiscuous binders exceeded the binding response of the positive control (Figure 3d,e). We applied strict selection criteria to minimize the number of false positives. Only fragments with binding response levels between 20% and 200% to that of DOC in CM5 and SA sensor chips and simultaneously displaying box-type kinetic responses were considered genuine hits. A total of 129 fragments matched these strict criteria (6.5% of total). These compounds were grouped into four family clusters according to their molecular structure (Supporting Information Table S3). A total of 44 fragments available with high purity from commercial sources were selected for in-depth characterization (Supporting Information Table S4).
